{{define "content"}}

JavaScript

Interactive components are Stimulus controllers. They work on any HTML: server-rendered pages, htmx swaps, or markup rendered by a client framework.

Loading

Each controller is an ES module named after it, such as tabs_controller.js, that exports the controller class. application.js starts the Stimulus application, and the CLI's main.js imports both and registers each controller under its identifier, so one <script type="module" src="/assets/js/velle/main.js"> is enough:

import { application } from "./application.js"
import TabsController from "./tabs_controller.js"
application.register("tabs", TabsController)

The controllers import {{.Site.Stimulus.Package}}, which velle does not ship. With a bundler, run npm install {{.Site.Stimulus.Package}}@{{.Site.Stimulus.Version}}. Without one, map it in an import map before any module script:

<script type="importmap">{ "imports": { "{{.Site.Stimulus.Package}}": "{{.Site.Stimulus.ESM}}" } }</script>

If your project already starts a Stimulus application, export it from application.js instead, or register velle's controllers wherever you register your own. Stimulus loaders that look for *_controller.js files pick them up as they are.

Or load the bundle, with the same import map. It starts an application, registers every controller and exports the application:

<script type="module" src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/codedbyshoe/velle-css@v{{.Site.Version}}/dist/velle.js"></script>

The bundle leaves out the adapters. To use one with the bundle, load its controller from dist/js/ and register it with the bundle's application:

import { application } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/codedbyshoe/velle-css@v{{.Site.Version}}/dist/velle.js"
import ChartController from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/codedbyshoe/velle-css@v{{.Site.Version}}/dist/js/chart_controller.js"
application.register("chart", ChartController)

Stimulus connects controllers when the page loads and whenever matching markup is added later, so nothing needs to be re-initialized after content changes.

Using the JavaScript without the CSS

The controllers work on any markup and don't need velle's stylesheets. To keep styles out of a project entirely:

velle init --js           # writes velle.json and main.js, and no styles
velle add tabs menu       # copies only their JavaScript
velle new controller cart # or start a controller of your own

Without the CLI, dist/js/ holds application.js and every controller on its own, and dist/velle.js is all of them in one module. Neither loads any CSS.

Styling is then yours. Controllers expose their state through ARIA and standard attributes such as aria-selected, hidden and open. A few also use class names or need a particular layout: each of those component pages says what it expects under Notes, and velle add prints the same note. Treat the data attributes on each component page as the controller's public API.

Attributes

The markup is standard Stimulus. Each controller has an identifier, such as tabs or check-all:

AttributePurposeExample
data-controllerConnects controllers to the element. Separate several identifiers with spaces.<div data-controller="tabs">
data-NAME-targetNames an element inside the controller's element that it uses. Several names can be separated by spaces.data-tabs-target="button"
data-actionConnects events to controller actions. Can sit on the controller's element or anything inside it.data-action="tabs#select"
data-NAME-OPTION-valueAn option read from the controller's element.data-tabs-index-value="2"
data-NAME-PARAM-paramA value passed to an action as event.params.PARAM.data-form-submitter-param="save"

Controllers can be nested. A target belongs to the closest element with the same controller.

Action syntax

[event[.keyfilter][@document|@window]->]NAME#method[:prevent][:stop][:self]
PartMeaning
eventAny DOM event name, including events controllers dispatch. When omitted, the element's default event is used: click for buttons and links, input for inputs and textareas (click for submit inputs), change for selects, submit for forms and toggle for <details>.
.keyfilterFor key events: only run for this key. Keys: any single letter or digit, or enter, tab, esc, space, up, down, left, right, home, end, page_up, page_down. Prefix with ctrl+, meta+, alt+ or shift+; modifiers must match exactly.
@document, @windowListen on the document or window instead of the element, e.g. for keyboard shortcuts and outside clicks.
:preventCalls event.preventDefault() before the action.
:stopCalls event.stopPropagation() before the action.
:selfOnly runs when the event's target is the element itself, not a descendant.

Separate several actions with spaces. The Stimulus reference has every option.

<textarea data-action="keydown.ctrl+enter->form#submit keydown.meta+enter->form#submit"></textarea>

Events

Controllers announce changes with bubbling events named NAME:EVENT, dispatched from the controller's element. Each component page lists its events.

document.addEventListener("tabs:change", event => {
  console.log("Selected tab", event.detail.index)
})

Writing your own controllers

velle new controller cart creates cart_controller.js to start from and registers it in main.js.

This example has a counter and a cart badge that follows it:

<div data-controller="counter">
  <output data-counter-target="output"></output>
  <button data-action="counter#increment">Add to cart</button>
</div>

<nav data-controller="cart" data-cart-count-value="0" data-action="counter:change@window->cart#refresh">
  <span class="badge" data-cart-target="badge"></span>
  <span data-cart-target="total"></span>
</nav>
// counter_controller.js
import { Controller } from "@hotwired/stimulus"

export default class extends Controller {
  static targets = [ "output" ]
  static values = { count: Number }

  increment() {
    this.countValue++
  }

  countValueChanged() {
    this.outputTarget.textContent = this.countValue
    this.dispatch("change", { detail: { count: this.countValue } })
  }
}
// cart_controller.js
import { Controller } from "@hotwired/stimulus"

export default class extends Controller {
  static targets = [ "badge", "total" ]
  static values = { count: Number, url: { type: String, default: "/cart/total" } }

  connect() {
    this.requests = new AbortController()
    this.loadTotal()
  }

  disconnect() {
    this.requests.abort()
  }

  refresh({ detail: { count } }) {
    this.countValue = count
    this.loadTotal()
  }

  countValueChanged() {
    this.badgeTarget.textContent = this.countValue
  }

  async loadTotal() {
    try {
      const response = await fetch(this.urlValue, { signal: this.requests.signal })
      this.totalTarget.textContent = await response.text()
    } catch (error) {
      if (!this.requests.signal.aborted) throw error
    }
  }
}

Values. countValueChanged() runs when the controller connects and whenever data-cart-count-value changes, whoever changed it, so it is the one place to render from. State lives in attributes, so CSS can read it directly:

[data-cart-count-value="0"] .badge { display: none }

Talking to other controllers. An action can listen for any event, so the cart follows the counter's dispatch() with data-action="counter:change@window->cart#refresh".

Reaching a controller from outside. application.getControllerForElementAndIdentifier(element, "cart") returns the connected instance, or null, for htmx hooks and inline scripts.

Several controllers on one element. List them in one attribute:

<form data-controller="form autosave" data-action="keydown.ctrl+enter->form#submit">

Saved copies of the page. Libraries that keep a copy of the page, such as htmx for its history, save whatever your controllers have added to it. If connect() builds markup that it would build again on the restored copy, define beforeSnapshot() to remove it and return a function that puts it back. The htmx extension calls it on every connected controller that has one:

beforeSnapshot() {
  const widget = this.widgetTarget
  widget.remove()
  return () => this.element.append(widget)
}

Everything else is plain Stimulus; the Stimulus handbook covers lifecycle callbacks, targets, values, classes and outlets.

Extensions

Extensions connect velle's controllers to other tools. They are optional, are installed only by name, and stay out of the bundles.

velle add htmx

Without the CLI, use the copy that matches how you load velle so it uses the same application: dist/extensions/ with the dist/velle.js bundle, or dist/js/ next to dist/js/application.js.

Each extension has a page under Extensions in the navigation.

Migrating from css-zero

The controllers are Stimulus controllers, as in css-zero, so most markup carries over. The differences:

css-zerovelle-css
data-local-time-target="ago" (inside a local-time controller)data-controller="local-time" data-local-time-format-value="ago" on each <time>
data-turbo-confirmdata-confirm

Each component page lists its targets, values and actions.
